learn.title: Types of values
learn.body: Every value has a type. Whole numbers are `int`, numbers with a decimal point are `float`, and text is `str` (a string). Text goes inside quotes, like `"hello"`.

learn.title: Math with numbers
learn.body: It prints 9, 3.5, 3 and 1. `/` always gives a `float`, `//` drops the decimals and `%` gives the remainder.
learn.code:
a = 7
b = 2
print(a + b)
print(a / b)
print(a // b)
print(a % b)

learn.title: Working with text
learn.body: It prints Hi, Ada then AdaAdaAda then 3. `+` joins text, `*` repeats it and `len` counts characters.

learn.title: Which type is it?
learn.body: Look for quotes and a decimal point.
steps: `7` has no point, so it is an `int`
`7.0` has a point, so it is a `float`
`"7"` is in quotes, so it is a `str`

learn.title: Mixing types
learn.body: You cannot add a number to text: `"age " + 5` is an error. Convert first with `str(5)`. Quotes change the meaning: `"5" + "5"` gives `"55"`, but `5 + 5` gives `10`.
Not sure of a type? Run `print(type(x))` and Python tells you.

questions.explanation: It has a decimal point, so it is a `float`.

questions.prompt: Match each expression to its result.
questions.explanation: Quotes make text, so `+` joins it. Without quotes `+` adds.

questions.prompt: To turn the number 5 into text, call \_\_(5).

questions.explanation: You cannot add text and a number. Use `"a" + str(1)` instead.
